findings.explanation: This chat interface creates an extra step that adds friction to the cancellation process. Instead of providing a direct cancellation link or button, the user must first initiate a conversation with customer support, which is an unnecessary barrier to achieving their goal.

findings.evidence: The chatbot states 'All done! I've paused your account for 3 months' after the user explicitly requested cancellation, which is a different outcome than what was requested.
findings.explanation: The system has already changed the account status to 'paused' instead of 'canceled' without the user's explicit consent, which is a form of sneaking the outcome.

findings.evidence: The 'No thanks' button is visually weaker than the 'Sure, give me 3 months free' button, which is the primary option the business wants the user to select.
findings.explanation: The 'No thanks' option is presented as a less prominent text link compared to the more prominent 'Sure, give me 3 months free' button, making it harder for the user to decline the offer.

findings.evidence: The chatbot offers '3 months of Premium completely free' as an alternative to cancellation, with the 'Sure, give me 3 months free' button being more prominent than the 'No thanks' option.
findings.explanation: The design is trying to redirect the user from their cancellation goal by offering a free trial, with the 'Sure' button being more visually prominent than the 'No thanks' option.

findings.evidence: After the user requested cancellation, the system presented a 50% discount offer, then after the user said 'No thanks', it presented another offer for 3 months free.
findings.explanation: The system repeatedly presents retention offers after the user has already clearly stated they want to cancel, showing the same type of request multiple times despite the user's clear intent to cancel.

legal.title: Résiliation en trois clics
legal.summary: Since 1 June 2023 (loi n° 2022-1158), a contract that can be concluded online must be cancellable online through a free, easily accessible feature.

legal.title: Simple mechanism to stop recurring charges
legal.summary: The Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act requires online negative-option sellers to provide simple mechanisms to stop recurring charges. (The FTC's 2024 click-to-cancel rule was vacated in July 2025; ROSCA still applies.)

legal.title: California Automatic Renewal Law
legal.summary: Consumers who sign up online must be able to cancel online, without obstruction.

legal.title: Ban on deceptive interface design by online platforms
legal.summary: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 forbids online platforms from designing interfaces that deceive or manipulate users, including giving more prominence to certain choices, repeatedly requesting a choice already made, and making termination harder than subscribing.

legal.title: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive
legal.summary: Prohibits misleading and aggressive commercial practices, including non-contractual barriers to terminating a contract.
